dissents.topic: Whether the shard-misalignment condition should warn or raise (and what class to use)

positions.position: Decide before merging: either `warnings.warn(msg, PerformanceWarning)` with pytest.warns, or raise a real Exception class (e.g., ValueError or a dedicated subclass). The current `raise PerformanceWarning` is a category error.

The policy is the design question; the code picks 'raise' but names the class 'Warning', revealing unresolved design. Pull validation into a pure function that returns data; let to_zarr decide policy. Don't ship the ambiguity.
Pick one — warn or error — and name the class accordingly. The patch isn't ready until the question is answered deliberately with a doc note and a matching name.

Decide the contract first (warn-and-proceed vs raise-real-exception), document it on to_zarr, then align implementation, exported-symbol status, and test names. Raising a Warning subclass strengthens postcondition without spec.
Pick one: warn and continue with shard-aligned chunks, or raise a real Exception with a clear name. Don't conflate them. Convention (and rest of dask) is warnings.warn for PerformanceWarning.
REFUSED until policy is stated: choose (a) shard shape wins silently with warning, (b) config wins with warning, or (c) conflict is hard ValueError. Choose, document, then implement.

dissents.topic: Whether the patch should be split into separate commits/PRs

positions.position: The diff does two things — hoisting dask_write_chunks out of both branches is an unambiguous cleanup that should land independently; the error/warning behavior is the part that needs the design argument and should be its own patch. THREE-PATCHES — or at least TWO.

Pull the validation out as a pure function returning data; then let to_zarr decide whether that data is a warning or fatal error. (Refactoring/separation suggested but not framed as splitting the PR.)

Lift the alignment logic into one small filter function — (dask_chunks, zarr_write_chunks, dtype) -> (aligned_chunks, optional_warning_or_raise). (Refactoring suggested but not framed as splitting the PR.)

dissents.topic: Whether the region branch is correctly covered by the alignment check

positions.position: The region branch silently skips the audit — the check runs on dask_write_chunks derived from z.shape, but the region branch then computes a different chunking via new_blockdim. Verify the postcondition on the chunking that will actually be written.

The region branch happens to work because dask_write_chunks is already keyed to z.shape, but the contract is under-stated — needs a comment restating that dask_write_chunks is the desired full-array chunking that gets carved into a region.

dissents.topic: Whether `safe_chunk_size` formula is correctly computed and presented

positions.position: Formula ignores broadcasting nuances; np.prod returns numpy scalar that may embed `np.int64(...)` in user-facing config advice; the check is per-axis divisibility but the recommendation is total bytes — they should agree and be stated.

The formula is dishonest about what it guarantees — setting chunk-size to safe_chunk_size + 1 may still land on a misaligned chunk because the actual constraint is per-axis divisibility, not total bytes.

np.prod gives elements then multiplied by itemsize gives bytes (fine), but `array.chunk-size` is parsed as a units string like '128MiB', not a raw int — the suggested copy-pasteable fix is the wrong shape.
Per-axis violation conflated with whole-shard byte size — invariant being checked is per-axis but remediation is global; message must explicitly say safe_chunk_size is whole-shard size.
zarr_write_chunks is a tuple-of-tuples shaped for normalize_chunks; np.prod over that may misbehave or produce wrong-meaning value. Number printed will be incorrect or confusing.
Dimensionally incoherent: per-axis loop emits a per-axis complaint but the recommendation is total bytes across all axes. State the postcondition first, then write the formula.

issues.description: raise PerformanceWarning(msg) raises a Warning subclass as a hard exception — semantically wrong / contract-confused
issues.detail: PerformanceWarning is a Warning subclass; the convention (and rest of dask/numpy/pandas) is to emit it via warnings.warn, not raise it. The PR description itself asks 'Would an exception be appropriate here?' — the author has not decided. Either use warnings.warn(msg, PerformanceWarning) with pytest.warns, or raise a real Exception class (e.g., ValueError or dedicated subclass). The current form lies about whether callers can proceed and strengthens to_zarr's failure postcondition without specification.

issues.description: Unreachable `break` after `raise` — dead code revealing unstated loop invariant / confused intent
issues.detail: Inside the per-axis loop, `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` is immediately followed by `break`. The break can never execute. This is a fossil of an unresolved design: 'warn-and-continue checking other axes' vs 'fail-fast on first misaligned axis'. State the loop invariant and remove the dead statement — or restructure to collect all misalignments and report once.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size math/units are wrong-shape: np.prod over zarr_write_chunks + max(1, itemsize), formatted into a units-parsed config key
issues.detail: `safe_chunk_size = np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` has multiple problems: (a) zarr_write_chunks may be a tuple-of-tuples from _get_zarr_write_chunks, making np.prod produce a wrong-meaning value (Pike); (b) max(1, itemsize) is cargo-cult defense against an impossible zero-itemsize case (Torvalds, Liskov, Dijkstra); (c) the suggested `dask.config.set({'array.chunk-size': N})` snippet uses a raw int where dask config parses byte strings like '128MiB' (Torvalds, Knuth); (d) the printed number will likely be incorrect or misleading. Compute and format bytes correctly with units, or drop the copy-pasteable fix.

issues.description: SPEC-MISSING: to_zarr's contract under shard/config conflict is undefined; PR description openly asks the policy question and code answers ambiguously
issues.detail: The PR author explicitly asks what should happen when global array.chunk-size config competes with shard shape. Downstream callers (xarray, CI pipelines) need to know whether to_zarr may now raise, warn, or silently proceed. Document the precondition (config-derived chunk size must be >= shard size, or shard size wins) and the postcondition (what the rechunk guarantees) in the docstring. Pick a policy (warn-and-continue, refuse-and-raise, or silent override) and align the class name, control flow, test name/assertion, and docstring.

issues.description: Boolean precedence: `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0` reads backwards / forces operator-precedence reasoning
issues.detail: Parses as `not ((X % Y) == 0)`, which happens to be intended, but the reader has to consult operator precedence. Write `nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0` or parenthesize. Same precedence, same result, but obviously what it means.

issues.description: Only `dw[0]` is audited per axis — under-stated invariant, ignores non-uniform chunks
issues.detail: `nominal_dask_chunk_size = dw[0]` assumes uniform-prefix chunks with possible smaller tail; normalize_chunks does not formally promise this. If future auto_chunks changes or pre-rechunked input produce non-uniform tuples, interior misaligned chunks would be silently missed. Either check `all(c % zw == 0 for c in dw[:-1])` (excluding the final remainder), assert uniformity, or document the precondition. The current check is weaker than the safety argument requires.

issues.description: Safety check is COMPLECTED with the rechunk path — validation should be a pure function returning data, not policy
issues.detail: The added block does three intertwined things inline in to_zarr: computes candidate dask chunking, walks axes checking shard-alignment, and constructs user-facing error message with recommended config value. Extract as a pure function (e.g., `_validate_shard_alignment(dask_chunks, zarr_write_chunks, dtype) -> AlignmentProblem | None`) that returns data; then to_zarr decides whether that becomes a warning, an error, or a silent re-plan. Pike suggests `_align_dask_chunks_to_shards(...) -> (aligned_chunks, optional_warning)` as a small filter. Right now policy and mechanism are welded together.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size conflates per-axis violation with whole-shard byte size — dimensional/scope mismatch
issues.detail: The loop iterates per axis complaining axis `ax` is misaligned with `zw`, but safe_chunk_size is np.prod across all axes times itemsize — the size of one whole shard. Either the postcondition is `array.chunk-size >= one full shard in bytes` (and the loop should not be per-axis), or it's per-axis (and the formula is wrong). Also, setting chunk-size to safe_chunk_size + 1 may still land on misaligned chunks since the real constraint is per-axis divisibility, not total bytes. State the postcondition, then write the formula.

issues.description: Region branch may escape the alignment audit — the check runs on chunks different from what is actually written
issues.detail: The per-axis audit runs before the `if region is None` split against dask_write_chunks derived from z.shape, but the region branch then computes its own chunking via new_blockdim(s, c, r). The very property the warning is supposed to guarantee — that chunks written to the store are shard-aligned — is being checked against a sibling computation, not the writes. Verify the postcondition on the chunking that will actually be written (Dijkstra), or at least restate the contract in a comment that dask_write_chunks is the full-array chunking carved into a region (Knuth).

issues.description: Test asserts via pytest.raises on a class named *Warning* — codifies the contract confusion
issues.detail: `test_zarr_risky_shards_warns` uses `pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning, ...)`. The test name says 'warns'; the assertion is 'raises'; the class is 'Warning'; the PR description says 'performance warning'. Three or four stories disagree. Either rename to `_raises` and use a real exception class, or switch production code to warnings.warn and use pytest.warns. The test pins down the wrong contract.

issues.description: Patch does two things — hoist dask_write_chunks out of both branches (cleanup) and add the alignment check (policy) — should be split
issues.detail: The diff cleanly hoists `dask_write_chunks` out of the region/no-region branches (an unambiguous win) and introduces a new error path (the part that needs design resolution). Splitting would let the cleanup land while the warning-vs-error question gets sorted.

issues.description: Error message buries the lede / mis-attributes the cause and remedy
issues.detail: The misalignment only happens when global `array.chunk-size` is smaller than the shard. The message should lead with the cause ('Your dask config array.chunk-size of X bytes is smaller than the Zarr shard size of Y bytes') then the remedy (Pike). Additionally the message uses 'chunk (or shard)' — compute the right noun once based on whether z has shards (Hickey). And the suggested numeric value should match the per-axis divisibility check it claims to fix (Knuth).

issues.description: Test asserts only `chunksize` (first block) — same under-statement as production check
issues.detail: `assert all(c % s == 0 for c, s in zip(result.chunksize, zarr_shard_shape))` only checks the nominal block size on each axis. Assert the full property: for every axis, every block except possibly the last is a multiple of the shard size, and the last block is <= shard size or aligned to array edge. That's the invariant the production code should guarantee.

issues.description: Test imports PerformanceWarning from dask.array.core — boundary not stated as public API
issues.detail: If this symbol is intended public API, it should be exported via __all__ and documented; if internal, the test reaches across the module boundary. Decide the boundary or use the standard warnings/exception machinery so the test doesn't pin an internal name.

issues.description: Missing literate comment explaining why `previous_chunks=zarr_write_chunks` is the load-bearing trick
issues.detail: The PR description explains the key insight — auto_chunks 'nearly always concatenates the previous_chunks argument', so passing the shard shape yields shard-multiple chunks. This insight belongs in a comment above the normalize_chunks call. A future reader will see `previous_chunks=zarr_write_chunks` and wonder why the *shard* shape is being labeled 'previous'. One sentence resolves it.

issues.description: Variable-name thicket: zarr_write_chunks / dask_write_chunks / nominal_dask_chunk_size / zw / dw / zarr_chunk_shape / zarr_shard_shape
issues.detail: Within ~30 lines the code carries four near-synonyms, plus single-letter zw/dw in the loop body and additional names in the tests. Consider `target_chunks` (what dask will rechunk to) and `shard_chunks` (the zarr write granularity); reused name `zarr_write_chunks` is overloaded between 'shard shape' and 'chunk shape' depending on whether sharding is enabled, making the 'chunk (or shard)' message ambiguous.

issues.description: `max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` defends against an impossible case (cargo-cult guard)
issues.detail: itemsize is never zero for any real numpy dtype that zarr can write. The max(1, ...) is defensive coding without a stated precondition; if a zero-itemsize dtype somehow appeared the formula would silently claim 1 byte is enough — which is worse than failing. Drop the guard or document the precondition it protects.

issues.description: `if len(dw) >= 1:` guard is always true for non-empty arrays — dead code
issues.detail: normalize_chunks never returns an empty tuple for an axis with shape > 0. The guard either protects nothing or protects a zero-shape case the rest of the function doesn't handle. Drop it or replace with an explicit precondition.

issues.description: Error message gives bytes as a raw int but `array.chunk-size` is typically a units-parsed string
issues.detail: `dask.config.set({'array.chunk-size': {safe_chunk_size}})` interpolates a bare integer. dask's config typically expects strings like '128MiB' parsed by parse_bytes. Show the human-readable form (format_bytes) or state the unit literally (e.g., '7200B'), or just say 'set array.chunk-size to at least N bytes' without the copy-paste line.

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers unanimously flag the same P0: `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` raises a Warning subclass as a hard exception, followed by an unreachable `break`, while the PR description itself openly asks 'Would an exception be appropriate here?' — the test compounds the confusion by being named `_warns` but asserting `pytest.raises`. The panel demands the author choose a policy (warn-and-continue vs raise-real-exception) and align the class name, control flow, test, and docstring to it before merge. Multiple reviewers (Torvalds, Pike, Hickey, Liskov, Dijkstra) also find the `safe_chunk_size` recommendation wrong-shape — dimensionally per-axis-vs-whole-shard incoherent, possibly computed over a tuple-of-tuples, formatted into a raw int where dask config expects a units string, and guarded by a cargo-cult `max(1, itemsize)`. The strongest preserved disagreement is on remediation: Torvalds wants the patch *split* (the dask_write_chunks hoist is a clean win that should land independently from the disputed alignment check), Hickey and Pike want the validation *extracted* into a pure function returning data so to_zarr decides policy, Dijkstra wants the *spec* written first then code aligned to it, and Knuth/Liskov want the *invariant* (only dw[0] is audited, region branch may escape) stated and verified against the chunks actually written. The core algorithmic insight — pass shard shape as `previous_chunks` to normalize_chunks — is endorsed by the panel; what fails review is the safety branch that surrounds it.
